summary: The root غلي primarily means to boil or bubble up, like water or a pot.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: غَلَتِ القِدْرُ, aor. تَغْلِى, inf. n. غَلْىٌ and غَلَيَانٌ, (S, MA, Msb, K,) The cooking-pot boiled; (MA, &c.;) and غَلِيَت, aor. تَغْلَى, is an unusual dial. var. thereof, the former being the more chaste; (Msb;) or غَلِيَت is not allowable. (S.) [Hence غَلَى said of a liquor, It estuated: it effervesced: it fermented: see نَبِي ٌ And hence] يَغْلِى دَمُهُ [as though meaning (assumed tropical:) His blood is fit to be shed ] is a phrase like رَابَ دَمُهُ, [q.

غَلَّىَ see 4, in two places. غلّى الرَّجُلَ, inf. n. تَغْلِيَةٌ, He rubbed the man over, or perfumed him, with غَالِيَة. (TA.) And غلّى لِحْيَتَهُ (Mgh, O,) Msb, all in art. غلف ) بِالغَالِيَةِ (O, ibid.) He daubed, or smeared, his beard with غَالِيَة; as also غَلَّلَهَا. (Mgh, O, Msb, ibid. [See 1 in art. غلف.]) And تَغْلِيَةٌ signifies also The saluting from afar, and making a sign. (K.)

اغلى القِدْرَ, (S, MA, K,) and, (K,) He made the cooking-pot to boil. (S, * MA, K. *) IDrd mentions, among some of the sayings of the people of former ages, أُنَّ مَآءً [ Pour thou out water, and make it to boil ]. (TA.) And one says, أَغْلَيْتُ الزَّيْتَ وَنَحْوَهُ [ I made the olive-oil and the like to boil ], inf. n. إِغْلَآءٌ. (Msb.)

تغلّى (S, Msb, K) بِالغَالِيَةِ (S, Msb) He (a man, S, Msb) perfumed himself, (S, * Msb, K,) or rubbed himself over, (K,) with غَالِيَة; (S, Msb, K;) and signifies the same; (IDrd, O in art. غلف;) as also تَغَلَّلَ, (Msb, and O in art. غلف,) and اِغْتَلَّ. (O in that art.)
تَغَاْلَىَ in all its sense, belongs to art. غلو, q. v.
غَلَانِيَةٌ, mentioned in the K in this art., belongs to art. غلو, being an inf. n. of the verb in the phrase غَلَا فِى الأَمْرِ. (TA.)
غَلَّايَةٌ A vessel of copper [or brass ], in which water is heated; thus called by the people of Syria; the same that is called مِحَمٌّ [q. v.] and قُمْقُمٌ and قُمْقُمَةٌ. (Msb voce قُمْقُمٌ.)

غَالِيَةٌ [ Galia moschata, ] a sort of perfume, (S, K,) well known; (K;) a certain compound of perfumes; (Msb;) musk mixed or boiled [ with other perfumes ]; (MA;) or a perfume composed of musk and ambergris and camphor and oil of ben: (KL:) it is said that the first who called it thus was Suleymán Ibn-'Abd-El-Melik; (S, TA;) and he did so because it is a compound boiled together upon the fire: or it was thus named by Mo'áwiyeh; the case being, that 'Abd-Allah Ibn-Jaafar went in to him, and…

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
